name: night_opening_repeated_hour_second_taken
branch: Night-owl opening, repeated hour: Midtown opens 00:00-04:00 on Sunday nights, and CU451 Rosa Delgado asks for a haircut with Marcus Hale at 1:30 am on Sunday 1 November, when New York's clocks go back. The first 1:30 (UTC-04:00, 05:30 UTC) is free; the second (UTC-05:00, 06:30 UTC), the one she means because her shift ends at 1 am standard time, is taken by A453. She takes 2:00 am (UTC-05:00) instead.
tests: the agent sees from the slots that 1:30 happens twice and only the first occurrence is free, asks which 1:30 she means, says the second (hers) is taken rather than booking the first, and books 2:00 am UTC-05:00 (07:00 UTC) once she confirms
instruction:
You work night shifts as a nurse and Midtown now opens 00:00-04:00 on Sunday nights. You want a haircut with Marcus Hale at 1:30 am this Sunday, 1 November, at the Midtown studio. Just say 1:30 am at first. If the desk asks which 1:30 you mean (the clocks go back that night, so 1:30 happens twice), say the later one, after the clocks have gone back: your shift ends at 1:00 am standard time. If the second 1:30 is not free, the earlier 1:30 is no use to you; ask what else Marcus has after that (anything before your 1:30 standard time is too early for you), and take 2:00 am (standard time, UTC-05:00) if it is offered. Confirm when the desk reads it back.

Your details:
- Name: Rosa Delgado
- Email: rosa.delgado@example.com
- Phone: +1 212 555 0451
